paragraphs.text: Judas (Jude): the name means praise or thanksgiving.

In humility, Jude did not mention that he was the brother of the Lord, that is, the son of His mother's sister, but said of himself that he was a servant of the Lord. He made known that he was the brother of James the son of Alphaeus, yet he did not mention that James was the bishop of Jerusalem, going further in his humility in order to hide his position and honor.

He sends his epistle to all the believers in the world whom God the Father has called and sanctified by His Holy Spirit, and whom He also keeps until the Second Coming so that they may be a bride for Christ. Thus he shows the relation of the Holy Trinity to the believers, whether of Jewish or Gentile origin, in their calling, their sanctification, and even their eternal happiness.
He asks for the believers the mercy with which they are distinguished, apart from the false teachers and their followers, of whom he will speak in this epistle.

He asks peace for them so that they may not be troubled by what these heretics do. Then he asks love for them also, as a grace from God, so that they may not condemn the heretics but love them, and hate their evil and their heresies.
Be discerning of evil and reject every strange thought, but at the same time have compassion on sinners and innovators, and pray for them.

(2) Departure from the faith and examples of it (vv. 3-7) 3 Beloved, when I gave all diligence to write unto you of the common salvation, it was needful for me to write unto you, and exhort you that ye should earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints. 4 For there are certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation, ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into lasciviousness, and denying the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ. 5 I will therefore put you in remembrance, though ye once knew this, how that the Lord, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed them that believed not. 6 And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day. 7 Even as Sodom and Gomorrha, and the cities about them in like manner, giving themselves over to fornication, and going after strange flesh, are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire.

The heart of the Apostle Jude was attached to the salvation accomplished on the Cross, in which believers from the whole world share, and he wished to speak about this subject, which always occupied him and in whose contemplation he delighted. But since he found innovators who had appeared in the Church, he was compelled to speak about the faith which the disciples and Apostles received once for all from Christ and which they hand on to their children, the faith by which we obtain this salvation and which protects us from all the deviations of the innovators. This faith includes the Holy Bible and all the teachings of the Church, that is, the Church's Tradition, which the spiritual fathers hand on to their children from the age of the Apostles until now.

The danger of these false teachers is that they are members of the Church and attack it from within with ideas foreign to it, spreading their heresies and evils among the weak and simple in order to deceive many. God knows them and has prepared for them judgment and eternal torment for their ungodliness, that is, their boldness in evil and their shameless spreading of their wicked ideas, and their proclaiming that they have secured the salvation they received from Christ, so that they rush into the sins of fornication and every uncleanness, claiming to be sure of their salvation. Moreover, because of their wickedness they deny the existence of God and the divinity of Christ, whether by words or by persisting in evil, as though He does not see them and will not punish them.

In order to warn the believers against the followers of the false teachers who claim to have obtained salvation, he gives them examples from the Old Testament in which some obtained salvation and then perished because of their evils. The first example in this verse is the people of the children of Israel, who were saved from bondage in Egypt and crossed the Red Sea, but murmured against Moses and refused to enter the Promised Land, and even wanted to return to Egypt. So they all died in the wilderness, and only two of them entered (Num 14:29). Likewise, when they worshiped the golden calf in the wilderness, God destroyed them (Ex 32).

The second example of the perishing of the righteous because of their lack of steadfastness in the faith is the angels, who had a high station in heaven and even presided over other angels and enjoyed the vision of God. But when they became proud and rejected faith and submission to God, they fell and lost their dwelling in heaven and became bound by sin, that is, darkness, until their eternal torment comes after the Day of Judgment.
Strange flesh: they fell into fornication and perversion, abandoning the natural bodily relations between husband and wife.
An example: a pattern of the punishment of the wicked.
Suffering the vengeance of eternal fire: their burning with fire is a prelude to the punishment of the eternal fire which their wicked inhabitants will suffer.

The third example is the inhabitants of Sodom and Gomorrah and the cities around them, who abandoned natural life and deviated into wrong bodily relations, that is, fornication and perversion, so they were burned by fire from heaven and will remain forever suffering the torment of the eternal fire.

Do not be careless about sin, relying on your knowledge or your outward connection with the Church, but repent quickly and humble yourself before God, and He will rescue you. And know that your relation to the Church ought to keep you even further from every sin.
Dominion: the authority of God.
Dignities: either the leadership of the Church or the angels and saints.
He speaks here about the false teachers who live in wicked dreams and keep far from the reality of the Church, her sound faith and her purity, so that they fall into graver sins, which are:
1- Uncleanness of the body, that is, fornication and all the evils connected with it.
2- They make light of the existence of God, that is, they reject the fear of Him, so they fall into many sins and do not hold fast to the faith handed down from the Fathers.

3- In persisting in their pride, they not only reject the authority of the Church but go so far as to attack her leadership with false accusations, and they may also condemn the saints who have departed, or the angels.

The Apostle mentions here a story known from ancient tradition, namely that after the death of the prophet Moses on the mountain, God hid his body so that the children of Israel would not worship it, because they were attached to him and loved him greatly. The devil tried to reveal his body in order to turn the people away from the worship of God, and the archangel Michael did not utter a word of condemnation against him by which to judge him and expose his evil, but said to him only, "The Lord rebuke thee," that is, may He restrain you from the evil you want to do. This is the conduct of the children of God who are steadfast in faith in Him.

On the other hand, in contrast with the conduct of the archangel Michael, we see these innovators speaking proudly against the angels and against the leaders of the Church, although they do not know the holiness and loftiness of these. And on the other side, in that in which they ought to have behaved well, like the animals, in bodily relations, in this too they became corrupt by falling into fornication and perversion, so that in their spiritual level they became lower than the animals.
He announces God's punishment of these false teachers because they walked in many evils, and he gives examples of them from the Old Testament, which are:
1- The way of Cain, which is lack of love for the brethren, for they deceived and led many astray by their corrupt opinions and destroyed them, just as Cain killed his brother Abel (Gen 4:5-12).

2- The error of Balaam for reward: the prophet Balaam advised Balak king of Moab to send women to commit fornication with the children of Israel so that God would forsake His people, and Balaam received from Balak many gifts as his reward for misleading and causing the people of God to stumble (Num 22-25). In the same way the false teachers led the believers astray by their corrupt ideas.

3- They perished in the gainsaying of Korah: Korah and those with him murmured against Aaron and his sons because they alone held the priesthood, and he said that all the children of Israel had the right to serve as priests, so the earth split open and swallowed him and all who were with him, 250 persons (Num 16:1-30). So also the false teachers who rebel against the Church will perish in eternal torment.

He describes the false teachers as obstacles that hinder the spiritual life of others, like the rocks in the sea that hinder the course of ships. These innovators attend the love feasts as members of the Church, but not to be bound in love with others; rather, it is to spread their corrupt teachings in order to hinder the faith. And when they hold love feasts, their aim in them is their own selfishness and the pleasing of themselves by misleading many so that they become their followers, and they spread their evil ideas in ungodliness, without fear or shame.

Likewise, they pretend to be godly, but they are like the clouds from which the farmer expects rain and is surprised to find them without water. So these teachers give no edifying spiritual word. He also likens them to autumn trees from which fruit was expected, since many trees bear fruit in autumn, but they have only leaves, and they are completely dead, so that it is best to uproot them since there is no hope in them. So these teachers persist in their sins and give no spiritual fruit, and there is no hope in them.
Foaming: having much foam, which is the white bubbles of water that the waves cast up on the shore, where they break and come to an end.

He likens their rebellion against the Church to the raging of the waves of the sea, which cast up the filth of the sea with their foam; they too, in their rebellion, cast their corrupt, stumbling ideas into the midst of the Church.

He also likens them to stars that should have given light, but strayed far from their course, so they lost their brightness and became dim and exceedingly dark. These too strayed from the teaching of the Church and lost the light of Christ that was in them, and nothing awaits them but the darkness of eternal torment.

Make use of the opportunity of your being in the Church to be bound to her, to love everyone and to submit to the life-giving teachings, and do not be content with the outward form of worship without putting God's word into practice, lest you lose the work of the Holy Spirit in you.

(4) Prophecies about the false teachers (vv. 14-19) 14 And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints, 15 To execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them of all their ungodly deeds which they have ungodly committed, and of all their hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against him. 16 These are murmurers, complainers, walking after their own lusts; and their mouth speaketh great swelling words, having men's persons in admiration because of advantage. 17 But, beloved, remember ye the words which were spoken before of the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ; 18 How that they told you there should be mockers in the last time, who should walk after their own ungodly lusts. 19 These be they who separate themselves, sensual, having not the Spirit.
He mentions here a prophecy taken from tradition about Enoch, the seventh descendant from Adam. This prophecy announces the coming of God on the Day of Judgment, surrounded by the holy angels.

On the Day of Judgment God will judge the wicked, especially those who boldly allow themselves in evil, not only for their evil deeds but also for every evil word they uttered and by which they caused others to stumble.
Murmurers, complainers: that is, grumblers.
Their mouth speaketh great swelling words: that is, with pride.
Having men's persons in admiration: hypocrisy and pretense.
He describes these wicked people as follows:
1- Murmuring and much complaining.
2- Indulgence in evil lusts.
3- Pride and arrogance in their words and conversation.
4- Hypocrisy and flattery of the great in order to gain their personal and material interests.

The Apostle Jude reminds the believers that, in addition to the prophecies of Enoch, there are prophecies of the Apostles about these wicked people, as mentioned in (2 Tim 1:3-5; Heb 2:1; 1 Pet 1:20; 1 Jn 2:18). These Apostles said that in the last time, that is, after the Lord Christ's ascension into heaven, there would appear reckless people who live as their evil desires and base lusts dictate to them and pay no regard to any spiritual or moral restraints.
Who separate themselves: they isolated themselves from the Church.
Sensual: they act according to their own whims. The soul here means the temperament and personal thinking, because man has spirit, soul and body.
Having not the Spirit: they are not submissive to the Holy Spirit but reject Him.
The Apostle continues his description of the wicked heretics, saying that they separated themselves from the Church, walked in their own mistaken thinking and refused to submit to the Holy Spirit.

Let you have your own opinion, but let it not be against the Church and her teachings, and take care to pray and to surrender your will to God before any matter, so that you may hear the voice of the Holy Spirit and receive the guidance of your father of confession.

(5) The foundations of the spiritual life (vv. 20-23) 20 But ye, beloved, building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Ghost, 21 Keep yourselves in the love of God, looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ unto eternal life. 22 And of some have compassion, making a difference: 23 And others save with fear, pulling them out of the fire; hating even the garment spotted by the flesh.
After warning the believers against the false teachers, he directs their attention to the positive work, which he defines in three matters:
1- Building up yourselves: he means spiritual striving and attention to good works.
2- On your most holy faith: that is, holding fast to faith in Christ, which turns into a life they live out in their inner feelings and in their conduct with those around them.

3- Praying in the Holy Ghost: prayer is what preserves a person's life and all his virtues, and for prayer to be sound it must be in the Holy Spirit, that is, by His work in them, so that He teaches them how to pray, guides them in what they ask and how they stand in prayer, and gives it warm spiritual feelings.

He also calls them to keep themselves from the cares of the world so that they may enjoy God's love in prayers and readings, and when they are filled with the love of God they are able to love those around them, however great their offenses. And even if they suffer some pains in this life, they have hope in the mercy of God, which compensates them for all their labors with the joys and glories of eternity.

If your goal is eternity, then care for the salvation of your souls and the souls of others, and help them to reach God by works of mercy and attention to their needs, but with discernment: you give tenderness and compassion if they are in weakness or despair, and firmness if they are in license and negligence.

He continues his talk about caring for the salvation of the souls of others and says that some of them need firmness. In order to save them from evil, they need to use warning and intimidation, and sometimes even punishment, so that they may be saved from the fire of evil that is in them, which, if they are slack in turning away from it, leads them to the eternal fire.

And he warns them, while they serve these reckless people, not to be defiled by their evils, but to keep away from everything connected with their sins and to remind them of them, like the garment worn by the fornicator during his fornication.

When you deal with others, remember that you are responsible for the salvation of their souls, so offer them your love and care for them in every way, and at the same time do not be ashamed to declare the truth so that they may pay attention to the salvation of their souls, even if they are annoyed with you for a while.

(6) Conclusion of the epistle (vv. 24, 25) 24 Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy, 25 To the only wise God our Saviour, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and ever. Amen.

He encourages the believers that God, the Lover of mankind, supports them in their striving and protects them from the sins of the world until they reach the day of true joy, which is their meeting with Christ in eternity, where they see His glory, His forgiveness and His love in the glories of heaven that He grants them.

He also encourages them that their God is wise and able to guide them in all their circumstances and direct them so that they may be saved from the evil of the world, and He is also the only God, so no power can stand before Him, but He is able to save us from every evil, so that we praise Him and glorify Him forever.

Trust that your God is strong and able to protect you from dangers, rescue you from every evil, support you however great your weakness, and complete your striving as long as you hold fast to Him, until He gives you to enjoy the joys of heaven with Him.
